svg.title: Random-walk MH vs HMC / NUTS
svg.desc: A random walk gropes without directional information and leaves heavy autocorrelation; HMC uses the gradient of the log posterior to trace Hamiltonian trajectories that travel far, and NUTS sets the trajectory length automatically.
svg.text: Directionless diffusion vs gradient-guided trajectories that travel far
Step ε, length L (auto in NUTS)
With no sense of direction it wanders back and forth
One trajectory carries it a long way
The gradient supplies direction, so it flows along the ridge
10,000 draws are worth only a few hundred independent ones
RW-MH gropes without direction and degrades sharply as dimension grows.
HMC traces gradient-guided trajectories far, and NUTS sets their length itself.
The more accurate the integration, the better H is conserved,
so even distant proposals are nearly always accepted
If divergent transitions appear, shrink the step size or reparameterize — next: convergence diagnostics.
